title: Sovereign Rule Engine: Self‑Healing Configurator for Residency & Retention
creator: Lin Zhao
description:
Goal: Build a reusable rule engine and operator (Sovereign Rule Engine) that continuously evaluates tenant residency and retention policies expressed in policy-as-code, automatically generates evidence bundles for audits, and performs safe corrective actions when configuration drift is detected. The operator should support declarative policy schemas, dry-run remediation, escalation handoff, and non-destructive rollback.

Background: We have several manual and ad-hoc remediation playbooks for residency and retention misconfigurations. Current gaps: slow detection windows, fragmented evidence collection, and lack of automated safe remediation resulting in manual intervention for region locks and retention overrides. This work ties into existing audit exporters and evidence streams but prioritizes an operator that can close the loop.

Scope:
- Implement a policy runtime that consumes policies (Rego or YAML-based rules) and evaluates live infra state + config metadata.
- Drift detection pipeline: snapshot configs, compute diffs, score drift severity, and persist findings to audit store.
- Remediation orchestrator: safe remediation actions (tagging, policy patch, route capacity changes, retention clamp) with pre- and post-checks and feature-flagged canary windows.
- Evidence automation: assemble tamper-evident evidence bundles (config diff, evaluation logs, runbook references, operator decisions) and export to S3 + compliance console.
- UX & control: expose remediation previews, approve/reject flows in Console, and a dry-run mode for new rules.
- Observability: metrics, SLO for detection-to-remediation time, and Slack/email incident alerts for high-severity events.

Non-goals: Rewriting existing audit exporters; this integrates with them. Not covering on-prem install mechanics in v1 beyond API compatibility.

Design notes:
- Policy format: adopt a normalized YAML policy manifest with optional Rego snippets for complex predicates. YAML allows non-engineer stakeholders to author simple policies.
- Evaluation cadence: default 10m for low-risk resources, 1m for high-risk (data residency controls).
- Severity model: severity = function(drift_type, resource_sensitivity, enforcement_status). Only P0/P1 events trigger automatic remediation; others create findings.
- Remediation model: three modes — notify-only, auto-remediate (safe actions), auto-repair-with-rollback (for reversible changes). Each action must have a compensating rollback plan and a TTL for automated rollback if downstream checks fail.

Implementation plan:
1) Policy schema & authoring API (2 wks): schema, validator, CLI validator.
2) Drift detector service (3 wks): snapshotter, comparator, scoring, persistence to audit DB.
3) Remediation orchestrator (3 wks): action registry, executor with concurrency limits, dry-run support.
4) Evidence bundler (2 wks): collate diffs, logs, signatures, and export pipeline.
5) Console integration & approval UI (2 wks parallel): remediation previews and approval workflow.
6) Telemetry/alerts & e2e tests (2 wks).

Risk & mitigations:
- Risk: False positives may cause unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: conservative defaults, dry-run, canary rollout to internal tenants first, and feature flags per org.
- Risk: Remediation causing side-effects across services. Mitigation: action safety checks, dependency gating, and required approvers for actions with cross-service impact.

Security & compliance: All evidence bundles signed with KMS-managed keys (integrate with existing KMS HSM), retention of evidence per org policy, tamper-evident manifests, and audit trail for operator decisions. Security review required prior to enabling auto-remediation for production tenants.

Success criteria:
- Reduce mean-time-to-remediate (MTTR) for residency/retention misconfigs from current baseline by 70% for P0 incidents.
- 95% of findings have a complete evidence bundle attached within 5 minutes of detection.
- No accidental cross-region data movement caused by remediation in canary group.

Rollout plan: Internal canary (redwood-internal tenants) -> beta customers who opt-in -> enabled by default for new small tenants -> enterprise enablement with SSO approvals.

Notes & links: Authoring spec draft in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COMPLIANCE/Sovereign+Rule+Engine (doc-in-progress). Initial proto PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1821. Audit store schema: docs/infra-audit-schema.md

acceptance_criteria: Policy manifest schema published and CLI validator available
Drift detector runs and produces findings for simulated drift tests
Remediation actions implement dry-run and can be toggled per-tenant
Evidence bundles produced for each finding and visible in Console
End-to-end e2e run that triggers a high-severity drift and performs safe auto-remediation in canary without impacting data residency
implementation_steps: Define YAML schema and authoring guide
Implement snapshotter for config and metadata
Expose policy authoring API and validation endpoint
Create action registry and implement safe action primitives
Wire evidence bundler to audit store and S3 export
Add Console preview and approval UX
Run internal canary and capture metrics for MTTR and evidence latency
